ny_beaverview.blurb: Beaverview is one of the bigger stretches of rock on Crane Mountain, a hill in the southern Adirondacks near Johnsburg and Thurman where the climbing is scattered across many small crags instead of one main cliff. The wall lies just east of the pond trail on the mountain's west side. Its eleven routes are nearly all trad, with a single top-rope line, and they stay moderate, running from about 5.4 to 5.8 with the bulk between 5.5 and 5.8. That makes it a reasonable place for newer leaders. The stone is solid but sees little traffic, so expect dirt, moss and sloping ground at the base of climbs. It feels remote even though towns are close.

ny_tooth_rock.blurb: Tooth Rock is a small boulder in Central Park, close to Cat Rock and the park's skating rink and pond. It is a short stroll from Cat Rock heading toward East Drive, with the boulder on your left. All eleven problems are bouldering, and the spread is wide for such a small block: a few easy V0 and V1 lines, a cluster around V2, then a handful of hard problems from V3 up to V6. It works as a quick stop on a city bouldering circuit rather than a destination, and it is one of the lesser-known blocks in the park compared with the larger boulders nearby.

ny_4_dave_s_wall.blurb: Dave's Wall is a compact cliff in the Tower Wall part of Powerlinez, in the southwest corner of Harriman State Park. It sits just west of the Three Bears slab, a short flat walk along the base of the Tower Wall. The face has interesting overhangs: the lower twenty-odd feet are steep, while the upper stretch lies back at a much gentler angle. Eleven routes split between trad and top rope, from around 5.6 to the low 5.12s, with most in the 5.9 to 5.10 range. Setting up top ropes means a careful scramble to the top and a long static line, and a couple of the harder trad lines carry run-out warnings.

ny_freefall_fringe.blurb: Freefall / Fringe is a cluster of boulders along Boulder Road in the Powerlinez bouldering zone of Harriman State Park. Boulder Road starts as a dirt road, climbs steeply at first and then eases off, and carries on toward other bouldering zones. The eleven problems here range from V0 up to V7, but most sit between V0 and V3, so there is plenty for newer boulderers, including an enjoyable right-leaning finger crack, with a few harder lines for strong climbers. Rock in the neighborhood is gritty and high-friction, tough on skin. Look for problems mostly along the uphill side of the road.

ny_c_the_clamshell_wall.blurb: The Clamshell Wall is the tallest face in the Dickie Barre section of Peterskill, the small Gunks-style cliff area in Minnewaska State Park. It is a mostly grey wall cut by many horizontal breaks, which gives it a look somewhat like the Trapps. About eight distinct lines follow vertical cracks and grooves, and the eleven routes listed run from 5.6 to 5.10, most of them 5.7 to 5.8. Nearly all can be led on trad gear or top-roped, with one top-rope-only line. A long static rope is handy for rigging from above.

ny_f_off_limits_reach_around_walls.blurb: Off Limits & Reach Around Walls is a section of Peterskill, a one-pitch area in Minnewaska State Park that is often called a miniature Gunks. The conglomerate here has roofs and horizontal cracks, and the eleven routes are mostly trad with a couple of top-rope-only lines. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.10, with a good number of easy to mid-grade climbs in the 5.6 to 5.8 range and just a few harder ones. Some top-rope anchors are bolted, and a few routes include bolts as well. It is a busy, popular spot that is frequently occupied on good weekends. Blazed trails lead along the base past neighboring walls.

ny_3_scheyichbi.blurb: Scheyichbi is a small crag in the Picatinny sector of Powerlinez, in the southwest corner of Harriman State Park. Ten routes are listed, a little over half of them top-rope and the rest trad. The range is unusually wide for such a small wall: a few easy 5.3 to 5.5 lines, a couple around 5.8, then a handful of hard ones from 5.10 to the low 5.12s. A standout undercling layback crack is the best-liked line on the wall. Rock in this area is typically sharp and gritty, and the roped cliffs here are short rather than tall.

ny_1_underking_sapokanikan.blurb: Underking / Sapokanikan is the first of the big boulders on Shakedown Street, in the Powerlinez bouldering zone of Harriman State Park. It is the leftmost formation in its group and holds a few classic highballs, so expect tall problems and plan for pads and spotters. Ten problems are listed, from V0 up to V6: a handful of easy lines, a few mid-grade problems, and several hard ones at the top end. The gneiss in this area is gritty and high-friction, rough on skin, and topping out tends to feel intimidating and committing, often over sloping holds.

_conflicts.ny_c_the_clamshell_wall: stored rock is sandstone, but the Peterskill page (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105896719/peterskill) describes the area's rock as quartzite conglomerate; the Clamshell page itself names no rock.
